chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan from Hisham ibn Salim said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram riding in the church (kanisah), so he said: 'No (it is not permissible), but it is permissible for women.'

key_terms.الْكَنِيسَةِ: The church (specifically referring to the Christian place of worship in this context)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a person in ihram to ride inside a church?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the gender-specific rulings for riding inside a church (*kanisah*) while in *ihram*, with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) permitting it for women but prohibiting it for men. This distinction reflects the practical considerations of modesty and ritual purity in pre-modern architectural contexts, where women’s riding styles or attire might differ from men’s in a way that affects the validity of their *ihram*. The ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh to accommodate gender-specific norms while maintaining the sanctity of the pilgrimage state.
